# FairFahren multiplayer race — conventions and harnesses

## When to Use

Use when working on the multiplayer/race implementation in the FairFahren repo
(`docs/plans/g-multiplayer/`, phases per `02-implementation-phases.md`), or any
touchpoint of `server/raceState.js`, `server/protocol.js`, `src/net/*`, or the
smoke tooling (`tools/smokeClient.mjs`). AGENTS.md owns the standing gates
(npm run check, review agent, size budget); this skill carries the parts those
gate bullets don't say.

## Procedure per phase

1. Read the phase's Deliverables + Tests sections and map each test name to the
   brief's acceptance line it satisfies — the test list IS the spec; write the
   test names before the module. Zero-dependency and pure-data rules from
   AGENTS.md apply; don't re-litigate them.
2. Adding/altering a message type: extend the `MESSAGES` registry in
   `server/protocol.js` FIRST (fields + validators — one shared encode/decode
   pair is driven by it), then run `node tools/protocol-table.mjs` and swap the
   table into NOTES.md between the markers. A unit test asserts the embedded
   table equals the generated one; skipping the regen fails check.
3. Keep side-effect ownership by injection: raceState gets `now/send/close/
   schedule`; src/net modules take every time source as an argument. Nothing in
   `server/` or `src/net/` may call `setTimeout` itself except `server/main.mjs`
   (the real-socket shell) — that is what makes the whole state machine testable
   on FakeNet's virtual clock.
4. Implement module + tests together (repo says speed over TDD ceremony), then
   `npm run check` BEFORE ending the phase: suite must not regress and the size
   budget must still pass (`src/net/*` COUNTS toward the client budget;
   `server/` does not).
5. End of phase: run the real-socket smoke (recipes in the reference), update
   NOTES.md (protocol table, decisions, how-to-test section), then run the
   review agent as AGENTS.md requires. Fix findings with a live repro first —
   see pitfalls.
6. Never commit or push unless asked; leave solo mode untouched — every phase
   must keep `npm start` behaving exactly as before the race work existed.

## Pitfalls

- **Callback slots are ASSIGNMENTS, not calls.** WsConnection/FakeConnection
  style APIs expose `conn.onMessage`/`conn.onClose` as settable properties:
  never write `conn.onClose(fn)` (calls a null slot; crashes the server on the
  first disconnect), and when a wrapper installs its own handler, wrap-and-void
  the existing one instead of overwriting it, or you get a ReferenceError (the
  wrapper's closure cannot see the caller's locals).
- **Close-reject order.** A race-state reject (`close(conn, 4000, ...)`) fires
  during `connect()`, before any client-side handler exists — capture reject
  codes in the test world's injected `close` wrapper array, not via onClose.
- **Joins race the start button.** Connect all fake/real clients in parallel and
  the early `start` (roster >= 2) closes the stragglers with 4001 mid-lobby —
  stagger joins (or start only when the roster is full) whenever a test/smoke
  wants everyone racing.
- **Relayed positions carry the SENDER's id.** When relaying `pos`, take the
  id from the sender's player record, not the receiver you are looping over —
  an easy variable-shadowing bug the receiver-side asserts will catch.
- **Finish reports accept `racing` OR `finished`.** Racers still on the road after
  the first finisher must be able to report (settle happens later); the guard is
  stage in {racing, finished} + once per player + no DNF flag. Accepting only in
  `racing` breaks the second finisher's report whenever the first flips stage early.
- **A new server→client type needs its client dispatch in the SAME change.**
  Adding a message to `server/protocol.js` without adding the handler case +
  `on.<event>` callback in `src/net/client.js` makes decode() accept it while the
  client drops it silently — the live feedback never fires and nothing throws.
- **Turn-away codes need re-delivery in tests.** A reject captured in the injected
  `close` wrapper must be re-delivered with its code by the test's client onClose
  handler — the peer side of a close is codeless, and a bare no-arg close maps to
  client stage 'dropped', so the 4000/4001 'turnedAway' states stay unreachable
  through FakeNet otherwise.
- **Rematch (`again`) wipes per-player state, including `gone`.** A racer whose
  connection died mid-race reappears on the rematch grid with a dead socket, and
  the fresh 30-s window settles them DNF again — that is the designed behavior;
  don't 'fix' the reappearance, and never reuse old-race finish data (seed bumps
  +1; finish/dnf/pen/gone all cleared).
- **Interp buffer contract.** push() ignores snapshots with t ≤ newest (never
  teleports backwards); sample() clamps at the newest snapshot — no extrapolation
  — and takes shortest-arc headings. Testing unordered input or extrapolated
  motion means testing the wrong contract.
- **Real WebSocket refuses send() before open.** createNetClient sends the join
  in its constructor; on a real socket that first call throws
  InvalidStateError and the page dies silently. The browser wrapper (main.js)
  must queue outgoing frames until 'open' and flush them then — FakeNet masks
  this because it queues itself.
- **Background tabs never run rAF.** When driving the real browser via the
  harness, a "dead" loop with empty HUD spans is usually the page being
  background-throttled, not a bug: call Page.bringToFront (or use new_tab) and
  re-probe before debugging.
- **Protocol wire format is FLAT.** Messages travel as `{type, ...fields}` —
  test drivers and smoke tools read `m.players`, not `m.data.players` (decode()
  re-adds `.data` only on the receiving side of unit code).

## See also

- `references/testing-recipes.md` — the fakeNet world() harness and the
  real-socket spawn driver for multi-player smoke runs.

{"content": "1|# 04 — Candidate brief
2|
3|> This is the document handed to candidates, together with the repository.
4|> (Interviewers: remove `docs/05-interviewer-guide.md` before sharing.)
5|
6|## Welcome to FairFahren 🚕
7|
8|You have a tiny 3D driving game: a Berlin taxi in a procedurally generated city. The whole game is about 50 KB of plain JavaScript — **no assets, no libraries, no build step**. Every building, tree and street comes from one seed number.
9|
10|Your job is to **extend it**.
11|
12|## Ground rules
13|
14|1. **Stay procedural.** Do not add image, model, audio, font or data files. Generate what you need in code.
15|2. **Stay small.** `npm run size` must pass (≤ 96 KB raw, ≤ 32 KB gzip for `index.html` + `src/`).
16|3. **No dependencies.** No npm packages, no CDN scripts — on the client and on any server you write.
17|4. **Stay deterministic.** World content must come from the seeded `Rng`, never from `Math.random()`.
18|5. **Keep it green.** `npm test` passes, and new logic comes with tests where it makes sense.
19|6. Small, focused commits with meaningful messages. We will read your history.
20|
21|## Getting started (≈ 30 min)
22|
23|1. Read [03-prerequisites.md](03-prerequisites.md), run `npm start`, drive around.
24|2. Read [02-technical-specification.md](02-technical-specification.md) and skim `src/main.js` — everything is wired there.
25|3. Try `?seed=7` and the `window.fairfahren` console object.
26|
27|## Tasks
28|
29|Pick **one main task** (or the one your interviewer gave you). Bonus tasks are optional.
30|
31|### A — Taxi missions (game loop) ★★
32|Turn the sandbox into a game. Spawn a waiting passenger (procedural figure + marker) at a random sidewalk spot, drive there and stop next to them to pick up, then deliver them to a destination shown on screen. Fare depends on distance and time; show money earned.
33|*Acceptance:* pickup only below 5 km/h within 4 m; destination reachable by road; fares and positions deterministic per seed + mission number; logic unit-tested without WebGL.
34|
35|### B — Traffic lights ★★
36|Add traffic lights at crossings (a pole with red/amber/green; bonus: the East-Berlin *Ampelmännchen* built from boxes). Cycle them per crossing so perpendicular directions never show green at the same time. Detect and display red-light violations.
37|*Acceptance:* state machine is a pure, tested module; lights are visible and readable at 50 m; violation is detected when crossing the stop line on red.
38|
39|### C — Minimap & navigation ★★★
40|Draw a minimap (2D canvas overlay) of streets, river and the taxi. Build a road graph from the city data and show the shortest route to a clicked destination (A* or Dijkstra).
41|*Acceptance:* the graph respects dead-ends at the river; route updates when the taxi leaves it; graph construction and pathfinding are tested.
42|
43|### D — AI traffic ★★★
44|Add 10–30 other cars that drive along the streets in the right-hand lane, turn at crossings and stop for obstacles in front of them (including the taxi).
45|*Acceptance:* no car drives through buildings or into the river; stays at ≥ 50 FPS; behaviour deterministic per seed.
46|
47|### E — A new district ★★
48|Add a new procedural block type with Berlin character — e.g. an elevated U-Bahn line (*Hochbahn*) on a viaduct along one street with stations, or a Kreuzberg-style street with *Spätis* and coloured awnings, or the Berlin Wall remnant with a strip of land.
49|*Acceptance:* integrated into `generateCity` via its own RNG fork; colliders where needed; invariant tests extended.
50|
51|### F — Better physics & feel ★★
52|Replace the kinematic model with a simple dynamic model: tyre slip, understeer/oversteer, handbrake drifts; body roll and pitch visible on the model; impact speed shakes the camera.
53|*Acceptance:* existing physics tests still pass or are consciously updated; new tests for slip behaviour.
54|
55|### G — Multiplayer race over the intranet ★★★★
56|Turn FairFahren into a short multiplayer race for **2–4 players** on different machines in the same network.
57|
58|**Flow**
59|
60|1. **Lobby.** One player starts the game server; the others open `http://<host-ip>:<port>/` and enter a name. Everyone sees who has joined (2–4 players, a fifth is turned away). Any player can press "Start" once at least two are in.
61|2. **Track.** A straight **200 m** race on a road of the city, e.g. eastwards along *Unter den Linden* from the gate. All clients derive the same track from the shared seed (the server picks the seed). Start grid with one slot per player, no taxi overlapping another.
62|3. **Start light (*Ampel*).** A traffic light above or beside the start line runs the German sequence **red → red + amber → green**. Cars are frozen until green. Every client must switch to green at the same moment (± 100 ms), regardless of network delay. Bonus: a jump start (moving before green) gets a time penalty.
63|4. **Race.** All players see all taxis moving in real time, smoothly, with a name tag. Each taxi is distinguishable (e.g. the player number on the roof sign or a coloured stripe — procedural, no textures).
64|5. **Finish line.** A visible chequered line across the road. Crossing it records the finish time (ms precision). The server, not the client, decides the official order.
65|6. **Siegerehrung.** When all players have finished (or 30 s after the winner), show the award ceremony to everyone: a podium with steps 1–2–3 built from geometry, the taxis placed on it, a camera orbit, and a results table with names and times. Then "Nochmal" returns everyone to the start grid.
66|
67|**Rules for this task**
68|
69|- The server is plain Node (`server/`), **zero dependencies** like the rest. Use the built-in `node:http`. You choose the transport — e.g. WebSocket via the HTTP `upgrade` handshake (RFC 6455, a few dozen lines), or Server-Sent Events plus `fetch` POSTs — and justify the choice in `NOTES.md`.
70|- The server serves the game files too, so players only need one URL. It listens on all network interfaces, not only `localhost`.
71|- The size budget still applies to the client (`index.html` + `src/`). Server code does not count.
72|- Single-player mode keeps working without a server.
73|
74|**Acceptance criteria**
75|
76|- Two browser windows on one machine **and** two machines in the intranet can race each other.
77|- The race state machine (lobby → countdown → racing → finished → ceremony) is a **pure module with unit tests**, including: start rejected with fewer than 2 players, fifth player rejected, finish order by time, a player disconnecting mid-race does not block the ceremony.
78|- The track (start grid, finish line) is generated from the seed and tested: 200 m long, straight, fully on road, no collider in the way.
79|- Other taxis move smoothly at 60 FPS even though network updates arrive at ~10–20 Hz (interpolation).
80|- The message protocol is documented (message types, fields, who sends what, at which rate).
81|
82|**Scoping.** This is the biggest task. In a time-boxed take-home, a solid result for steps 1–5 with two players beats a shaky all-in version; note in `NOTES.md` what you left out and how you would add it.
83|
84|### Bonus (small, any time)
85|- Headlights toggle (`L`) and a day/night cycle in the shader.
86|- Horn (WebAudio, synthesised — no audio files).
87|- Spatial grid for collision queries + a micro-benchmark.
88|- Gamepad support.
89|- Camera that does not clip into buildings.
90|
91|## What we look for
92|
93|Clean, readable code that fits the existing style; sensible decomposition (pure logic vs. rendering); tests for logic; respecting the constraints; and being able to **explain your trade-offs**. A smaller, solid result beats a large, fragile one.
94|
95|## Hand-in
96|

{"content": "1|# NOTES.md
2|
3|Working notes for the multiplayer task (task G, `docs/04-candidate-brief.md`):
4|what was built, what was cut and why, how to test it. The work follows the
5|phased plan in `docs/plans/g-multiplayer/02-implementation-phases.md`; this
6|file grows with the phases and is completed at hand-in.
7|
8|## Transport: WebSocket, hand-rolled (RFC 6455)
9|
10|The race needs traffic both ways constantly: every player streams their taxi at
11|~15 Hz while the server pushes everyone else's positions, the lobby roster and
12|the shared start-gate moment. WebSocket is one open phone line per player —
13|either side talks whenever it wants, a few bytes of overhead per message.
14|
15|The alternative considered was Server-Sent Events (a server→client radio) plus
16|one `fetch` POST per client message. Less code, but every position update from
17|every player becomes its own HTTP request: more latency noise, more churn per
18|tick, and no clean way to push "the other taxi moved" at 15 Hz. On top of that,
19|the project's zero-dependency rule takes a WebSocket library off the table — so
20|the handshake (SHA-1 accept key) and the framing live in `server/ws.js`,
21|unit-tested against the RFC's own example bytes.
22|
23|## Wire protocol
24|
25|JSON text frames tagged with `type`. Messages are tiny and the intranet is
26|fast, so readable beats compact. All times are milliseconds in the shared
27|server clock; clients learn their offset from the app-level `ping`/`pong` pair
28|(the browser's WebSocket API hides the protocol-level ping/pong from
29|JavaScript, so RTT measuring has to live in the application messages).
30|
31|A join into a full lobby is not a message: the server closes the socket with
32|close code 4000 and reason "lobby full". A connection arriving while a race is
33|already running is closed with 4001 "race already started". The client shows
34|its turn-away screen from the close code (groundwork for the lobby UI in
35|phase 3).
36|
37|<!-- protocol-table:start -->
38|| type | from | fields | rate |
39||---|---|---|---|
40|| join | client → server | name | once, on entering the lobby |
41|| name | client → server | name | on change, in lobby |
42|| start | client → server | — | user-triggered |
43|| pos | client → server | x z h s | 15 Hz while racing |
44|| finish | client → server | t | once per race |
45|| jump | client → server | — | user-triggered, before green |
46|| again | client → server | — | user-triggered, in ceremony |
47|| ping | client → server | t | about 1 Hz while syncing |
48|| roster | server → client | players seed | on change |
49|| countdown | server → client | goAt | once per race |
50|| go | server → client | goAt | once per race |
51|| posRelay | server → client | id x z h s | per player, 15 Hz |
52|| stage | server → client | stage | on change |
53|| disconnect | server → client | id | on player leaving |
54|| pong | server → client | t s | on ping |
55|| finishInfo | server → client | id t | per finisher, once |
56|| jumped | server → client | id pen | per jump, once |
57|| results | server → client | players | once, when the race is settled |
58|<!-- protocol-table:end -->
59|
60|The table is generated from the definitions in `server/protocol.js`
61|(`node tools/protocol-table.mjs`); a unit test fails if this file and the code
62|drift apart. `finishInfo` announces each finish as it happens (for a live
63|position HUD); `results` is the settled, ordered table
64|`[{id, name, t, dnf}]` — finished players first in official order (time, ties
65|to the earliest report), DNFs last with `t: null`.
66|
67|## Phase 2 — the rules, all pure
68|
69|Every rule of the race lives in `server/raceState.js`: a pure module that
70|gets its clock (`now`), its transport (`send`/`close`) and its timers
71|(`schedule`) injected, so the tests drive whole races — joins, start gate,
72|position relay, finishes, results, ceremony — over `fakeNet` pairs with a
73|virtual clock, no sockets and no real time. Key decisions:
74|
75|- **The server settles everything.** A finish report carries the client's
76|  crossing time, but the official order is the server's sort: by reported
77|  time, ties to the earliest report. A lying or lagging client can shuffle
78|  itself but not the podium.
79|- **Disconnects never block the ceremony.** A racer that drops is marked DNF
80|  and stays on the results table (`t: null`); when the 30 s window after the
81|  winner expires, anyone still on the road is settled as DNF too.
82|- **One shared `goAt`.** The countdown and the go message both carry the same
83|  server timestamp; clients compare it against the master clock (`src/net/clock.js`)
84|  and flip green when *it* arrives, not when the packet does.
85|- **The track is pure data** (`src/net/track.js`): 200 m east on Unter den
86|  Linden from just past the gate's first crossing, grid seats side by side in
87|  the racing lane, chequered line, ampel position — all validated against the
88|  city colliders at build time, and identical for equal seeds.
89|- Found and fixed while wiring: `conn.onClose(...)` in `main.mjs` *called*
90|  the callback slot (always null on a fresh socket) instead of assigning to
91|  it — the real-socket path would have died on the first disconnect. The
92|  review pass added the remaining hardening: a race where everyone quits
93|  before any finish settles at once (no winner was coming), late finish
94|  reports after the results are out are ignored (they would contradict the
95|  podium clients already received), negative finish times are dropped, and
96|  the main.mjs port argument survives `--seed` in either order.
97|
98|## Where the multiplayer code lives
99|
100|- `server/main.mjs` — the game server: serves the static game exactly like
101|  `npm start`, speaks WebSocket on `/ws`, listens on all interfaces (`0.0.0.0`).
102|- `server/static.mjs` — static file serving, extracted so the dev server
103|  (`tools/serve.mjs`) and the game server share one implementation.
104|- `server/ws.js` — pure RFC 6455: handshake, frame encode/decode, masking,
105|  ping/pong, close. Small unfragmented frames only (our messages are tiny).
106|- `server/protocol.js` — the message language: one entry (direction, fields,
107|  rate) per message type, one shared encode/decode pair driven by the entries.
108|- `server/fakeNet.js` — in-memory server/client pairs with controllable
109|  latency and drop, so the race rules (phase 2) are testable without sockets.
110|- `server/raceState.js` — the rules as one pure state machine: lobby →
111|  countdown → racing → finished → ceremony, roster and start gate, finish
112|  order, ceremony trigger, DNF handling.
113|- `src/net/clock.js` — master-clock maths: offset from pong samples,
114|  min-rtt-of-N filtering, `serverNow()`. Pure, DOM-free.
115|- `src/net/track.js` — pure `buildTrack(city, playerCount)`: the 200 m start
116|  straight, grid seats (validated place-only against colliders), finish line,
117|  ampel position.
118|
119|## Phase 3 — players on each other's screens
120|
121|The online presence layer: `?online` in the URL opts a browser into net mode
122|(solo `npm start` never opens a socket and looks exactly as before — the lobby
123|panel and overlays stay hidden). The browser wiring lives in `src/main.js` +
124|`index.html`, the pure parts stay in `src/net/`:
125|
126|- **Lobby.** `createNetClient` joins immediately on construction — the join
127|  button press builds the client (that IS the connection trigger, plus name):
128|  a wrapped `WebSocket` with `{send, close, onMessage, onClose}` slots. The
129|  index.html overlay shows the join form while connecting, then roster (with
130|  per-player colour dots), a start button that is disabled until `canStart`,
131|  and a status line. The whole lobby hides once the race starts; while waiting
132|  the local taxi is parked, not drawn and never stepped.
133|- **Self id by join order.** The server never names us in a roster, but we
134|  only receive rosters once *our* join is subscribed, and in that first
135|  broadcast we sit last in join order — the client takes the last row of its
136|  first roster as its own id. Duplicate names cannot break this (it is order-
137|  based, not name-based).
138|- **Seed handoff.** `seedChange` (fired exactly once per distinct seed) →
139|  `generateCity` + `buildCityMesh` + re-upload happen synchronously. The
140|  "Warming up…" full-screen overlay was cut: the whole rebuild is ~1–2 ms
141|  (~23 ms for the city build was our upper-bound estimate), less than a paint,
142|  so a flashing overlay would only add a visible glitch.
143|- **Remote taxis.** Every `posRelay` is pushed into a per-peer
144|  `createInterp` buffer (t = local receive time); each frame samples ~100 ms
145|  behind the render clock and draws the *same* `buildTaxi` meshes again with a
146|  per-player matrix. Distinguishing riders is a thin coloured skirt under the
147|  ivory body plus the lobby legend dots (roster index → one fixed 4-colour
148|  palette, identical on every client). Peer drop → interp removed.
149|- **Track.** `buildTrack(city, playerCount)` runs client-side, re-keyed by
150|  `seed/rosterLength` so a roster-size change (or a new city) rebuilds before
151|  the next countdown, and only for 2–4 players.
152|- **Cut:** in-world name tags — 15 extra mini-boxes per rider ×4 players was
153|  more mesh + draw calls than the size budget wanted to carry for something
154|  the colour stripes + roster legend already answer; also no auto-reconnect
155|  (turn-away/drop shows a clean "Reload" screen instead).
156|
157|## Phase 4 — race day
158|
159|- **Grid + freeze.** First sight of stage `countdown` wipes the last race's
160|  bookkeeping (remotes, jumps, finishes, results), rebuilds the track and
161|  regrids: local car `Object.assign(car, createCar(gridSlot))` on
162|  `rosterIndex(selfId)`, camera snapped, `R` keeps respawn (to the slot once
163|  one exists). Physics runs through `createStartGate` around `stepCar` — a
164|  pure freeze, not an input hack; pressing the throttle pre-green reports
165|  `jump` once via `sendRaw`, the server settles `+3000 ms` and broadcasts
166|  `jumped` (client.js now has the `jumped` case → `on.jumped`, shown live as a
167|  HUD chip and a ⚡-style sentence in the results).
168|- **Ampel.** A static mesh (dark pole, housing, dim lamp sockets) plus ONE
169|  mesh per light state at `track.ampel`; each frame only the active state is
170|  drawn, driven by `ampelState(clock.serverNow(), goAt)`. While red the HUD
171|  chip counts down the seconds to the shared `goAt`.
172|- **Finish.** Each physics step in `racing` compares prev/current (x, localT)
173|  via `crossingTime(…, track.finish.x)`; on a crossing the local time is
174|  converted with `clock.serverNow()` (falls back to local now while unsynced)
175|  and reported once through `sendFinish`. Live position HUD: `P1 + count of
176|  others who crossed before you`, replaced by the settled order once `results`
177|  arrive.
178|- **Results + ceremony.** `results` rows display `((t − goAt)/1000).toFixed(2) s`
179|  (t is an absolute server stamp) plus ` +{pen/1000} s` when the server
180|  penalised a jump start; DNF rows stay as "DNF". Stage `ceremony` builds the
181|  three podium steps from `podiumLayout`, parks the settled taxis on their
182|  steps (DNF-row taxis on the ground row), and the camera orbits the step
183|  centroid (radius 14 m, height 6 m). The **Nochmal** button sends `again`
184|  (only legal in ceremony) — the server bumps its seed by one, everyone gets
185|  `roster` + `stage countdown` again and the same loop regrids onto the NEXT
186|  world. `client.js` got one extra line for this: `finishSent` resets when a
187|  fresh `countdown` arrives, so the rematched race can report a finish again.
188|- **Turn-away / drop.** Close codes reach `on.turnedAway(code)`: 4000 →
189|  "Stadt voll — versuch es später wieder", 4001 → "Rennen läuft schon — versuch
190|  es gleich nochmal", any drop → "Verbindung verloren." — each with a Reload
191|  button (`location.reload()`).
192|
193|## How to test on two machines
194|
195|1. `node server/main.mjs --seed 42 8081` on one machine (serves the game AND
196|   the WebSocket on the same port, listening on `0.0.0.0` — `ipconfig` for the
197|   LAN IPv4).
198|2. Every player opens `http://<host-ip>:8080/?online`, types a name and presses
199|   **Mitfahren**. Rosters match on all screens, and every screen regenerates
200|   the same city (same seed + street names in the HUD).
201|3. Someone presses **Start** (needs ≥ 2 riders) → everyone's ampel counts down
202|   from the shared `goAt` and flips red+amber → green "at once". Holding the
203|   throttle before green costs that player +3 s in the results.
204|4. Race east along Unter den Linden (~200 m), watch each other's taxis drive
205|   smoothly, cross the line → live position, then the results table and the
206|   podium orbit; **Nochmal** throws everyone onto the next seed's grid.
207|5. Closing a tab mid-race settles that rider as DNF on the podium; a fifth
208|   tab gets the turned-away screen (4000/4001); killing the server shows the
209|   "Verbindung verloren" screen.
210|6. Regression: plain `http://<host-ip>:8080` (no `?online`, no server needed)
211|   must drive exactly like `npm start` did before phase 1.
212|
213|## Status
214|
215|Phase 1 (server foundation) done: the server serves the game, speaks WebSocket,
216|the whole message language is defined, and later phases run their tests over
217|`fakeNet`. Phase 2 (game rules) done: `npm test` drives entire races through
218|`raceState` over the fake network — start gate, roster, relay, finish order,
219|DNF ceremony, 30 s force, clock maths and per-seed track invariants — all pure
220|and browser-free. Next: the client core (phase 3), then race day (phase 4).
221|Solo mode is untouched: `npm start` works exactly as before, and the client
222|budget is unaffected by the server (the size check covers `src/` +
223|`index.html`, now 58.3 / 21.4 KB of 96 / 32 KB).
224|
225|## How to try phase 2 by hand (zero browsers)
226|
227|`npm test` owns the rules; for the real socket path:
228|
229|- `node server/main.mjs --seed 42 8081` in one terminal, then two or three
230|  `node tools/smokeClient.mjs Alice 8081` (name + port) in others. Watch:
231|  rosters appear on everyone's side, the race refuses to start with one
232|  player, positions flow once green, finishes are ordered by reported time,

235|- A fifth player running `node tools/smokeClient.mjs Eve 8081` after the race
236|  starts gets `closed 4001 race already started`; connecting a fifth before
237|  the race gets `4000 lobby full`.
238|
239|## How to try phase 1 by hand
240|
241|- `node server/main.mjs`, then open `http://localhost:8080` in two tabs — the
242|  game must load and drive exactly like `npm start` does.
243|- From another machine on the same LAN: `http://<host-ip>:8080`

247|  → expect `HTTP/1.1 101` and `Sec-WebSocket-Accept: s3pPLMBiTxaQ9kYGzzhZRbK+xOo=`.
248|  (Unit tests cover the frame bytes; curl only proves the handshake path.)", "total_lines": 248, "file_size": 14894, "truncated": false, "is_binary": false, "is_image": false, "not_found": false}
